notes: Vanilla wowsims does not model an Arcane-specific preset (the fork's mage/apls/p1.apl.json is Fire, ui/mage/apls/forever_frost.apl.json is Frost), so this was built from Forever's own Arcane talent tree plus a community guide, not a direct port. Fix round 1: two of this guide's own lines are presently inert in this engine build and are kept anyway per the fix-round-1 controller ruling, so the file states the intended design and upgrades itself once the engine catches up -- (1) Arcane Blast (400574): sim/mage/talents.go says outright the package does not register this spell yet; (2) the Missile Barrage gate on Arcane Missiles (400589): no aura is ever created under that id, because this package's Arcane Missiles channel is not re-costed/re-timed for the proc (also noted in sim/mage/talents.go). Both lines cast nothing today -- `notes` on each says so -- and an unconditional Arcane Missiles cast is added at the bottom of the priority list as the engine-castable Era filler that keeps this rotation actually dealing damage in the meantime; Era Arcane (before Arcane Blast existed) was itself an Arcane Missiles-spam rotation, so this is not a downgrade in spirit, only in ceiling. Arcane Missiles' own top rank (25345, rank 8) is also excluded by an off-by-one in the engine's registration loop (sim/mage/arcane_missiles.go: `for rank := 1; rank < ArcaneMissilesRanks; rank++`, so rank 8 never registers); every Arcane Missiles reference here uses 10212 (rank 7), the highest rank the engine actually registers, with the missing rank 8 recorded as an engine follow-up. Arcane Power and Presence of Mind are both confirmed castable and are kept on cooldown, off the GCD-costing category, ahead of a specific nuke. Every rank named here (other than the two flagged inert conditions) is checked against the spellconst of the newest client build in builds/. Rotation-accuracy program diagnosis (2026-09-28), inert 1239696 and 400589: Arcane Blast (sim/mage/arcane_blast.go) and Missile Barrage (sim/mage/missile_barrage.go) are both fully implemented now -- the two per-line notes below already say so -- but every rank of Arcane Blast beyond rank 1 (1239696/1239697/1239699/1239700) and every one of Missile Barrage's proc ids (400588/400589/401736/467409) are absent from talents/mage.json's own ranks[].spell_id table, which only names rank 1 (400574) as 'the id this talent point grants'. The ladder harness's talent-zero-points exemption (talentSpellIDs) therefore only recognizes 400574 as talent-gated, not the ids above it in the same chain or the proc aura id, even though registerArcaneBlastSpell gates EVERY rank on the same single Talents.ArcaneBlast bool. At level 30 exactly (the first level Arcane Blast rank 2's own RequiredLevel(30) would let it register) the ladder's own truncated talent walk has not yet reached that node, so the engine correctly does not resolve 1239696 -- and by level 38 it has (the golden's own level-38 cast set shows spell:1239696=41.2, the dominant cast), so this is not a persistent engine bug, just a harness talent-chain-tracking gap that happens to land exactly on level 30's rung. Missile Barrage (400589) shows the identical shape at levels 10 and 20, clear by level 30. Fix round: 1239696 is not declared inert here after all -- the pinned engine resolves it fine once both the level and the talent are met (confirmed by the level-38+ rungs of the ladder, and inert would have wrongly told the level-60 zero-talent smoke test to expect it unresolved, which it is not, since spellranks.json alone -- ignoring the talent -- already treats a level-60 character as having every rank). Fixed instead in sim/request/ladder.go: expandTalentSpellIDs widens the harness's zero-points exemption from talents.json's single named id per node (400574 only) to every id spellranks.json's own 'Arcane Blast' rank grouping shares with it, so rank 2 (1239696) is recognized as gated by the same talent rank 1 is. 400589 (Missile Barrage) stays declared inert: it is a bare aura id with no ranked chain at all (spellranks.json's four rows are all rank 0), so there is no ability-name grouping for expandTalentSpellIDs to walk, and it is never referenced by a level-60 zero-talent smoke run either way (the smoke build's own Missile Barrage condition is untalented and silent, not warned). Rotation-accuracy program, wand-weaving addition (2026-09-28): Shoot (5019) is declared inert because this build's item table has no wand with required_level <= 10, so the level-10 rung equips nothing in the ranged slot and core.RegisterShootSpell never registers the spell there; it resolves and fires heavily at levels 20 and 30 (64.9 and 68.2 percent of top casts) before Arcane Blast's mana efficiency keeps this bare-gear character's mana comfortably above Shoot's 20 percent threshold for the rest of a 300-iteration run -- see the expected_idle entry below for why it goes quiet again from level 38 on, not a regression. Rotation search (2026-10-07, after the engine began charging Arcane Blast its client price of 15% base mana plus 175% per stack): a stack-gated pair of Blasts followed by a Frostbolt filler measured about 10% above the old unconditional Blast line; six stack/filler candidates were measured by hand (one to three Blasts, Missiles or Frostbolt filler) because the search's mutations cannot write a stack gate.

engineering_notes.3: Missile Barrage (400589) is the talent proc the engine registers since 2026-09-28.
engineering_notes.4: The client rank chain is 400574..1239700 (levels 20/30/40/50/60 per spellranks.json); this file names the top rank and the level rewrite picks the learned one. The engine registers the chain since the accuracy program (engine-caster lane). Rotation-accuracy program correction (2026-09-28): this note previously said the 1239696..1239700 portion covers levels 40..60 -- spellranks.json actually puts rank 2 (1239696) at level 30, not 40; see the top-level notes' inert entry for the level-30 harness gap this produces.
engineering_notes.5: Uses the top rank (25345, rank 8); the engine's rank loop registers all eight since 2026-09-28.

expected_idle.reason: Once Arcane Blast is talented and learned (level 30+ on this build), its mana efficiency keeps this bare-gear character's mana comfortably above the 20 percent threshold core.RegisterShootSpell's Shoot line is gated on for the rest of a 300-iteration run, so it never fires from level 38 on. Not a defect: the level 20 and 30 rungs already show it firing heavily (64.9 and 68.2 percent of top casts) before Arcane Blast takes over.

Wowhead Classic: Arcane Mage DPS Rotation, Cooldowns, and Abilities

priorityList.notes: Arcane Power on cooldown: a flat 30 percent damage cooldown with no cast time of its own.
Presence of Mind on cooldown: free (no GCD) and makes the next cast instant.
Missile Barrage is the talent proc that empowers your next Arcane Missiles cast -- fire the empowered Missiles under it, where the Arcane guide places the payoff.

Arcane Blast twice, never a third time: the client charges it 15% of base mana and each stack of its own buff raises the next cast's cost by 175% (the buff also makes every other spell hit harder while it stands, up to four stacks), so the second Blast is affordable and the third is not. Cast your current highest learned rank.

Frostbolt is the filler once two Blasts are up: a cheaper, faster cast than Arcane Missiles that still enjoys the Blast buff on your other spells and still has a 20% chance to proc Missile Barrage. Casting it ends the Blast buff, which is the point - the next Blast starts a fresh, cheap pair. Before Arcane Blast is learned, Arcane Missiles spam is the whole rotation.
Shoot with your wand once mana falls under 20%: it costs nothing and keeps damage going while you regenerate, and Wand Specialization adds to it.
